socialTrends.name: Real-pumpkin spice
socialTrends.desc: People can taste the difference between pumpkin puree and pumpkin-spice syrup. Still the seasonal default.
socialTrends.ponderSpin: You already bake. A Texas-style PSL with a pinch of cayenne is on-brand and easy to story.

socialTrends.name: Brown sugar shaken espresso
socialTrends.desc: Still the most copied iced drink. Brown sugar, shaken espresso, oat milk.
socialTrends.ponderSpin: Use the same brown-sugar note as the cinnamon rolls so the drink and the pastry rhyme.

socialTrends.name: Maple cold foam
socialTrends.desc: Maple foam on cold brew or chai photographs well and feels like fall without being pumpkin-only.
socialTrends.ponderSpin: Pecan + maple is the North Texas version. Toast the pecans for the smell in the truck.

socialTrends.name: Honey chai
socialTrends.desc: Chai with local honey instead of syrup. Simple, warm, not a science project.
socialTrends.ponderSpin: Call it Ponder honey chai and put the beekeeper on the chalkboard.

socialTrends.name: Pistachio mocha
socialTrends.desc: The pistachio-chocolate wave from last winter is still selling as a fall mocha.
socialTrends.ponderSpin: One weekend special is enough. If it moves, keep it through football season.

spring.name: Lavender Honey Latte
spring.desc: Espresso with local honey, steamed milk and a touch of lavender syrup. Light and floral.
spring.tip: Top with dried lavender buds for a pretty presentation.

spring.name: Texas Pecan Cold Brew
spring.desc: Slow-steeped cold brew with house-made pecan syrup and a splash of oat milk.
spring.tip: Use locally sourced pecans for that real Texas flavor.

spring.name: Strawberry Matcha Lemonade
spring.desc: Iced matcha layered over fresh strawberry puree and sparkling lemonade.

spring.name: Cinnamon Roll Latte
spring.desc: Inspired by your famous scratch-made cinnamon rolls — cinnamon, brown sugar, cream cheese foam.
spring.tip: Pair with an actual cinnamon roll for the ultimate combo deal.

spring.name: Honey Bee Flat White
spring.desc: Velvety flat white sweetened with raw local honey and a light dusting of cinnamon.
spring.tip: Source honey from Denton County beekeepers for a hyper-local story.

spring.name: Mint Mocha Iced
spring.desc: Rich chocolate mocha poured over ice with fresh mint and whipped cream.
spring.tip: Muddle real mint leaves for a garden-fresh twist.

summer.name: Watermelon Agua Fresca Coffee
summer.desc: Cold brew meets fresh watermelon agua fresca — surprisingly refreshing.
summer.tip: Perfect for 100+ degree days. Serve in Mason jars.

summer.name: Coconut Vanilla Cold Brew
summer.desc: Smooth cold brew, coconut cream and Madagascar vanilla over crushed ice.
summer.tip: Freeze coconut milk into cubes so it never gets watered down.

summer.name: Peach Sweet Tea Espresso
summer.desc: A true Texas fusion — sweet peach tea with a shot of espresso over ice.
summer.tip: Use Hill Country peaches when in season.

summer.name: Mexican Horchata Latte
summer.desc: Creamy cinnamon-rice milk horchata mixed with espresso. Sweet and spiced.
summer.tip: Batch the horchata base daily for consistent creaminess.

summer.name: Frozen Caramel Macchiato
summer.desc: Blended espresso with caramel, vanilla and milk — frozen to perfection.
summer.tip: Drizzle caramel inside the cup for a beautiful spiral effect.

summer.name: Blueberry Lemon Cold Brew
summer.desc: Bright blueberry compote and lemon zest stirred into nitrogen cold brew.
summer.tip: Garnish with a lemon wheel and a few fresh berries.

fall.name: Pumpkin Spice Latte (Texas Style)
fall.desc: Real pumpkin puree, warm spices, espresso and steamed milk. No artificial stuff.
fall.tip: Add a pinch of cayenne for a subtle Texas kick.

fall.name: Maple Pecan Cappuccino
fall.desc: Rich cappuccino topped with maple syrup foam and candied pecan pieces.
fall.tip: Candy the pecans in-house — they smell amazing.

fall.name: Apple Cider Chai
fall.desc: Hot apple cider blended with spiced chai concentrate. Autumn in a cup.
fall.tip: Rim the mug with cinnamon sugar for that extra fall feeling.

fall.name: Salted Caramel Mocha
fall.desc: Dark chocolate mocha with house salted caramel and a flaky salt finish.
fall.tip: Use Maldon sea salt flakes — the crunch makes it special.

fall.name: Brown Sugar Oat Latte
fall.desc: Espresso with oat milk and torched brown sugar syrup. Cozy and sweet.
fall.tip: Brulee the brown sugar on top with a kitchen torch for drama.

fall.name: Sweet Potato Pie Latte
fall.desc: Roasted sweet potato puree, warm spices, espresso and marshmallow cream.
fall.tip: A Southern classic turned coffee drink — pairs with cinnamon rolls!

winter.name: Gingerbread Latte
winter.desc: Warm ginger, molasses and cinnamon espresso with whipped cream and cookie crumbs.
winter.tip: Serve with a mini gingerbread man perched on the rim.

winter.name: Peppermint White Mocha
winter.desc: White chocolate mocha with real peppermint and crushed candy cane topping.
winter.tip: Use white chocolate shavings on top for an elegant touch.

winter.name: Mexican Hot Chocolate
winter.desc: Rich dark chocolate, cinnamon, a hint of chili and topped with whipped cream.

winter.name: Eggnog Espresso
winter.desc: Creamy eggnog steamed with espresso and a dusting of fresh nutmeg.
winter.tip: Offer a dairy-free version with oat-based nog.

winter.name: Cranberry Orange Americano
winter.desc: Bright cranberry syrup and orange zest over a classic hot Americano.
winter.tip: Garnish with a dehydrated orange wheel — gorgeous and shelf-stable.

winter.name: Fireside S’mores Mocha
winter.desc: Chocolate mocha with graham cracker crumbs and toasted marshmallow cream.
winter.tip: Toast the marshmallow with a torch tableside for a fun experience.
